title: "Intermediate R"
subtitle: "Session - Row numbers and dates"
---

## Adding a row number

::: {.incremental}
- Very useful for calculating times between things
- or identifying things like referral time to second contact and so on
:::

```{r}
library(NHSRdatasets)

data <- NHSRdatasets::ae_attendances

data |>
  dplyr::filter(org_code %in% c('RQM', 'RJ1', 'RDD')) |>
  dplyr::arrange(org_code, type, period) |>
  dplyr::mutate(row_number = dplyr::row_number())
```

## Row number per org_code

```{r}
dat <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(org_code %in% c('RQM', 'RJ1', 'RDD')) |>
  dplyr::arrange(org_code, type, period) |>
  dplyr::mutate(row_number = dplyr::row_number(), .by = c(org_code, type))

View(dat)
```

## Row number per date (dense rank)

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::filter(org_code %in% c('RQM', 'RJ1', 'RDD')) |>
  dplyr::arrange(period) |>
  dplyr::mutate(row_number = dplyr::dense_rank(period))

```

## Reverse dates

Whilst it's possible to put a '-' in front of the variable if it's an integer

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::arrange(-admissions)
```

This doesn't work with dates:

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::arrange(-period)
```

## Reverse ordering dates uses a dplyr function

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(period))

# compare to the default ascending order

data |>
  dplyr::arrange(period)
```

## Row number per date - jump missing (rank)

```{r}
dat <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(org_code %in% c('RQM', 'RJ1', 'RDD')) |>
  dplyr::arrange(period) |>
  dplyr::mutate(rank_row_number = dplyr::min_rank(period)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(row_number = dplyr::row_number(period))

View(dat)
```

## Using `between()`

Now lets remove 2018 by using the first and last date

```{r}
dat <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(org_code %in% c('RQM', 'RJ1', 'RDD')) |>
  dplyr::filter(!dplyr::between(
      period, # note the ! in front for the between to convert it
      # into a not between
      as.Date('2018-01-01'),
      as.Date('2018-12-31')
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(period)

View(dat)
```

## Over to you

Adjust the code above to:

- remove the year 2017 and 
- return only the first 3 rows 
- for only type 1 
- for each organisation

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
countdown::countdown(
  minutes = 10,
  color_border = "#005EB8",
  color_text = "#005EB8",
  color_running_text = "white",
  color_running_background = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_text = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_background = "white",
  margin = "0.9em",
  font_size = "2em"
)
```

## Answer - adjusting code

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::filter(
    org_code %in% c('RQM', 'RJ1', 'RDD'),
    !dplyr::between(
      period, # note the ! in front for the between to convert
      # it into a not between
      as.Date('2017-01-01'),
      as.Date('2017-12-31')
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(org_code, type, period) |>
  dplyr::mutate(row_num = dplyr::row_number(), .by = org_code, type) |>
  dplyr::filter(row_num <= 3)
```
